title: Finite free point models and quantitative dual Tor bounds
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A=R/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $u\leq v$ be integers and let $N\in D^b_c(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be intrinsically bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] with Tor amplitude in $[u,v]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $C=\operatorname{Fib}_sN=\Gamma(s,N)$ for its ordinary module complex [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Then $C$ has finite cohomology modules and ordinary-module Tor amplitude in $[u,v]$: $H^i(C\otimes_A^LM)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[u,v]$. In the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C$ is isomorphic to a complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules with $P^i=0$ outside $[u,v]$. Its derived dual $C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A)$, with derived Hom specialized to the one-point ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], is represented by the signed Hom complex with degree $i$ term $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-i},A)$. Thus $C$ and $C^\vee$ are perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and $C^\vee$ has finite cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[-v,-u]$.

proof.text: The finite coefficient ring is finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to identify the uniformizer ideal with the maximal ideal. Its positive power is proper, so the quotient is nontrivial and local; transport along ULift. A finite ring is Noetherian. The finite cohomology assertion for C is already part of the codomain property of the recorded pointFiniteFibre [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-point-sections-tor-amplitude] to the intrinsic Tor hypothesis. The sections object is definitionally the underlying object of pointFiniteFibre, so transport along the supplied equality with C. This proves the ordinary Tor interval [a,b], including tests by arbitrary coefficient modules.

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: The Tor interval gives cohomology concentrated in [a,b]. Finite underlying cohomology modules are finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to obtain pseudo-coherence, then [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to obtain a bounded finite-term projective model Q. Apply [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] to Q, with the original Tor interval, to obtain a finite free model P supported precisely in [a,b]. Compose its derived isomorphism with Q to obtain C isomorphic to Q(P).

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: Finite free terms are projective. Apply [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] to P and A[0], and contravariantly transport internal Hom along C isomorphic to Q(P). The degree-i Hom cochain is determined by its only possibly nonzero component P^(-i) to A[0]^0; evaluation at that component and the single cochain construction are mutually inverse. The existing Hom-complex differential formula gives (-1)^(i+1) times precomposition with d_P. Thus the dual model D is supported in [-b,-a]. Its terms identify with ordinary module duals of the finite free terms of P, hence are finite free.

source.place: Step 1: geometric-point passage, finite free models, and reversed-degree duals

proof.text: The two bounded finite free models exhibit perfectness [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Apply the bounded flat-complex theorem [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude] to D and transfer along the dual-model isomorphism. Each finite-generated D term over a finite ring is a finite set. Its cycles embed in that finite set, and its homology is a quotient of cycles, so homology is finite. Vanishing outside [-b,-a] supplies finite cohomological support.
